CORRECTED 2026-10-11 FROM THE LEAD'S FIELD EVIDENCE - THE STOP WORKS; THE BADGE DOES NOT CLEAR, and that is the defect. First filed as "the Stop does not stop it", which was WRONG about its central fact. The state, read from GET /api/screen after the fact: state "ended", on false, paused null, left_s null, ended "owner", ended_words "you stopped it" - the backend had ALREADY ended the session before the read. The badge window was still on screen ten minutes later saying "Jarvis is watching - paused" and "Paused: one of Jarvis's own windows - 8 min left", its Stop still offering to stop nothing, while the number it showed counted down on its own. THE HARM IS THE SIGN ITSELF: a stale "Jarvis is watching" badge is a FALSE PRIVACY ALARM, in the one feature whose whole promise is a visible sign plus an instant stop, and the owner will act on it. CAUSE, TRACED - the badge is EVENT-ONLY after startup and never re-reads: watch-badge.js:156 listens for the screen-status event, :161 reads screen_status ONCE at startup, and render() re-schedules itself every 10 s while sign.on and current() decrements left_s LOCALLY from the last payload - which is exactly why a frozen payload looks alive, with a decreasing countdown. The desktop emits screen-status only when THE APP ITSELF makes the call (look.rs:551-552 run_watch -> on_status -> :468 emit_all), and on_status hides the badge only in its else-if-was branch after BADGE_ENDED_FOR, 15 s (look.rs:476-485). So ANY ending that does not come through this app's own screen_watch command - another client, the voice or quick "stop watching" path (screen_stop), the countdown running out on the PC, a watchdog - leaves the badge up for ever. Two readings of this field case remain, and each is testable: either the ending came from a path that emits nothing, or it came from the app and the event never reached the badge window's listener. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS ALREADY ON THE SCREEN: the bar and the tray follow the SAME on_status, so if the Jarvis bar still shows a watching sign, the app never learned; if the bar cleared and only the badge is stale, the event reached the app but not the badge window. Also noted: ended "owner" is the string ENGINE.stop() writes (jarvis_screen.py:1312-1314), so the ending was a POST /api/screen stop and not the hotkey, whose stop_everything() writes "stop_all" (:1649). ALREADY REFUTED, kept for the record: the paused state is not the cause (jarvis_screen.py:1310 and :1646 both end a PAUSED session) and the verb is accepted from anywhere (ANY_DOS :1814). NOT CHANGED AND NOT TO BE CHANGED: the pause rule and the sign's wording behaved correctly. WHAT A FIX MUST DO, and it is not done here: the badge must be able to learn the session ended WITHOUT this app being the one that ended it - a status re-read on the same 10 s tick it already runs, with the existing 15 s ended display then closing it.
